rationale: Round 1 built cleanly with no ICE and correct execution, so this round raises SecurityGain across the board to push obfuscation coverage while keeping the cost dimensions high enough to steer passes away from the hot compute kernels (eamForce, ljForce, timestep, haloExchange) that dominate CoMD runtime. FLA gets the highest SecurityGain (0.9) because control-flow flattening is the strongest structural defense and the large cold functions (printPerformanceResults, main, initEamPot parsing/setup) are ideal hosts; BCF is second (0.8) but with the highest RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights (0.85) so it concentrates on cold code rather than inflating the inner loops. ICALL (0.8) and IGV (0.7) harden call-graph and data-structure reconnaissance in this pointer-heavy MPI-style proxy app, with CorrectnessRisk held at 0.85/0.8 to be conservative around the function-pointer tables and halo-exchange plumbing. SPLIT and SUB are cheap enablers — high DiversityGain (0.8/0.85) and low cost weights let them apply broadly, breaking basic-block boundaries and instruction signatures to amplify FLA/BCF effectiveness with minimal overhead. IBR (0.75) adds branch-level indirection at a moderate threshold, avoiding the tightest loops via its RuntimeCost weight.
